Title: Source 1: Survey finds U.S. schools start ‘too early’
Author: by Ashley Yeager
Content: It’s `text(8 a.m.)` and the `text(first)` school bell rings. Some students zip through the halls. Others bumble along. It’s a common scene starting again across the United States. And it’s happening a bit too early in the morning for most tweens and teens, a new survey finds.

Starting school too early is not just a student complaint. It’s an observation backed by science, says Anne Wheaton. She works at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, [GA]. As an epidemiologist, she [examines] the causes behind health problems. Her focus has been health problems linked with teens’ lack of sleep.

For a new study, she and her `ultext(colleagues)` looked at the start times of an estimated `text(39,700)` U.S. public schools during the `2011-2012` school year. The average start time was `text(8:03 a.m.)` . . .

That’s too early, Wheaton says. Tweens and teens are experiencing shifts in their natural sleep cycles. Their bodies’ inner “clocks” make it hard for them to go to bed before `10:30` or `text(11:00 p.m.)` But to get to school on time, they have to wake up as early as `text(5:30 a.m.)` A first school bell just after `text(8 a.m.)` slices into the `8.5` to `text(9.5 hours)` of sleep tweens and teens need to be healthy and perform at their best, she says. . . .

Indeed, Wheaton’s colleagues at CDC published a major `ultext(analysis)` in Pediatrics last `text(year)` about all of the problems teens can experience if they get too little sleep. Janet Croft of CDC (a coauthor on the new paper, as well) concluded: U.S. schools “start at such an early time that most teens are essentially brain dead when they go to these early classes.” . . .
The call for later school start times is an essential movement for keeping tweens and teens healthy. . . .

Wheaton says she and her colleagues understand that the change in school start times is not going to happen overnight. The goal, she says, is to make sure everyone knows how important sleep is and that school start times can greatly affect how much sleep `ultext(adolescents)` get each night.

:box:`bbtext(Glossary)`

colleagues: people who work together

analysis: a careful study or explanation

adolescents: teenage boys and girls
